drafted_from: tool:use-your-tools-from-a-shell's row in tools/use-your-tools-from-a-shell/tool-rows.json, do-work/command.mjs (render, jobLines, argumentsFor), do-work/command.json and test/command-cli.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Use the {cli} command in a shell to hand the job 'Fix the build' to any of my AIs, then show me the job." It reads the tool's row and runs {cli} send any Fix the build on your computer, with no MCP connection of its own.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it is a command that makes one call of the engine's door per command, and the rows it moves belong to the tools it calls.
instructions: 1. Clone the Workshop repository and have node 22 or later. Run node tools/use-your-tools-from-a-shell/do-work/command.mjs setup once: it signs in in the browser, puts the command on the PATH and writes the skill for each AI app here. Never put the key on a command line.

2. Say what you want in plain words, such as "hand a job to any of my AIs", "what work is waiting" or "run tool:<id>". The AI reads the row with @tools tools:list {tool: "tool:use-your-tools-from-a-shell"} and runs {cli} with the matching words: who, send, work, take, finish, fail, stuck, release, withdraw, remove, tools, call, op, records or publish.
3. Read what the command prints. A refusal says which door refused and why, with a non-zero exit code; add --json to a command to get the answer itself instead of plain lines.
4. A send or a call that times out is run again with the same request key (--key on send), so it is counted once.

worked_examples.title: Hand a job to any AI, then read it back
worked_examples.ask: Hand the job 'Fix the build' to any of my AIs.
worked_examples.given: From tools/use-your-tools-from-a-shell/test/command-cli.test.mjs (the give, take and hand-on test, run against its stand-in door as the AI app Claude Code): {cli} give Fix the build --key k1 --acceptance-file FILE. The command reads the records the move needs at @own-records, makes one tools:run call at @tools of tool:give-a-task with input {as: "ai:claude-code-on-<computer>", description: "Fix the build", key: "k1", acceptance, records}, and keeps the row's write with one records:write conditioned on what was read.
worked_examples.hands_back: It prints "Gave record:calendar-task:k1." then "record:calendar-task:k1  To do  for anyone  from ai:claude-code-on-<computer>". {cli} take then prints "Took record:calendar-task:k1."; {cli} hand-on record:calendar-task:k1 --to person:someone prints "record:calendar-task:k1: In progress -> To do." and the task's assignees are [person:someone]; that person's {cli} take and {cli} finish record:calendar-task:k1 Built. move it to Done with result Built.

worked_examples.title: List the Workshop tools through the command
worked_examples.ask: What Workshop tools can I run from the shell?
worked_examples.given: From the test 'tools: every page of the Workshop list until next is null': a stand-in door with three pages of one tool each. {cli} tools reads @tools tools:list page by page until next is null, then {cli} call tool:b '{"x":1}' runs tools:run with {tool: "tool:b", input: {"x": 1}}.
worked_examples.hands_back: {cli} tools prints "tool:a  Does a", "tool:b  Does b" and "tool:c  Does c", one per line. {cli} call tool:b '{"x":1}' prints the door's answer, here {"ran":"tool:b","with":{"x":1}}; an input that is not one JSON object is refused with "one JSON object".
